Passionnée de vulgarisation? Racontons l'histoire fantastique des rovers! 

Des milliers d'idées ne demandent qu'à être libérées le 14 novembre.

Rejoignez cette équipe à vos risques et périls.... :-)
summary:
From Mars to the Moon and beyond, rovers, probes, and satellites have transformed our understanding of the universe through remarkable discoveries. This project is a tribute to their legacy and to the fascination they continue to inspire.
Through a series of interactive books, children can embark on extraordinary adventures alongside our rover friends as they explore distant worlds. Each book is dedicated to a real space mission, bringing science and exploration to life in an engaging and accessible way.
Whether they are just beginning to read or already confident readers, every child can enjoy the stories at their own pace, with the option of audio narration to guide them along the journey.
The platform is fully optimized for both smartphones and computers, making exploration possible wherever curiosity leads. No internet connection? No problem. Every book can also be downloaded as a PDF for offline reading.
Join our rover companions and discover the wonders of space, one mission at a time.
details:
What tools, coding languages, and software did you use?

 Esveille is a lightweight online reader, built in HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No installation, no account: a family opens a link, and the story begins.

 Its features were designed for young readers and their parents:

- Bilingual reading: children switch between French and English at any moment, on any page.

- Audio narration on every page, with free play and pause, so children who cannot read yet are never excluded.

- Display modes: single page or double-page spread, faithful to the feeling of a real book.

- Offline export: the complete 32-page book, the cover, two pages per key moment, then the credits, can be downloaded as a PDF, with the pictures and the book's text kept as real text, so the story travels everywhere, even far from any connection.

 Development followed a deliberate, human-directed process. Our technical lead wrote the design brief, defined the architecture of the website, and organized the rounds of coding to be as efficient as possible while respecting the foundation set at the start of the project. The code was written by an AI agent under his direction, including the selection of the animation, sound and PDF-transformation libraries, and he reviewed each iteration and carried out rounds of testing to deliver a website as functional as possible in the limited time we had.

 

Rather than adopting a ready-made reader library, we chose to direct the AI agent toward a result we could fully shape on a tight schedule. That decision cost us time; it bought us control. Because we master our platform from A to Z, we control how the media meet on each page: how the drawing holds the text, how the voice follows the words, and how the book can leave the screen. The container is not a shell around our content: it is part of the story we tell.

 

What makes Esveille different?

- The content. Story, illustrations, audio: every medium is made by hand, by us. In a market flooded with generated content, every page of Esveille can be traced back to a human gesture: a sentence, a drawing, a voice.

- The approach. Vulgarisation through accessibility: real mission history, told with the very words scientists chose themselves, narrated aloud so that no child is excluded by their reading level.

- The languages. Every story exists in French and in English, side by side. We want language learning to be a by-product of wonder: a child absorbed in the story of two rovers is learning a language without noticing it. Developing new languages in children is not a feature of Esveille, it is one of its raisons d'etre.

- The container. We built the reader ourselves, so nothing stands between our intentions and the child's screen. The media mix, the navigation, the offline PDF: all of it is ours, designed end to end.
